Give us just the numbers -- that is to say, the number first and then the name, like you see it on the list.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me see: Number 3, Hakija Srna -- no, not Hakija, no, not Hakija. Osman Jasarevic was there, number 5. Seljakovic was brought in but was released when Simo -- ah, Hajrudin. I'm mixing up their names. One of them was returned to the 4th Detachment, as his surname was Seljakovic. Now, whether it was Hajrudin or not, I'm not sure. I also know Enver Ibralic. No, the rest weren't. None of the others were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: My question was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, remember to pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question was: Which of these people were incarcerated together with you in the TO and the primary school, and not whether you know them.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jasarevic, Osman, nicknamed Roma.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, Mr. Salkic: You know Mr. Sulejman Tihic, do you not?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: He was the president of SDA of Bosanski Samac at that time, was he not?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Fuad Jasenica?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: He was a member of the SDA, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Izet Izetbegovic, the founder of the SDA party in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What about Alija Fitozovic? You know him too, don't you?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the course of your testimony, in the transcript of the 31st of October, page 3186, line 4 and 5, asked by my learned colleague the Prosecutor whether you were ever a member of any political party, you stated the following: "No, no, until about one year prior to the war, when I joined the SDA political party, and I stepped down from the party six months later." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, give or take a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But that's the statement you made here, is it not?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That could mean that sometime at the end of 1991 you ceased to be an SDA member.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On that same LiveNote, of that same page, line 22, 24, asked by the Prosecutor once again whether you had taken part in any party activities, such as meetings and the collection of funds or similar activities, your answer was in the negative.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that is my same answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So by that you mean no?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mean no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salkic, that means, if I understood you correctly, that while you were a member of the SDA party, you did not procure any equipment for the party, did you?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If you didn't procure anything while you were an SDA member, I assume that you didn't procure anything like that when you ceased to be a member.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I never did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is it not true, Mr. Salkic, that in April 1992 - or more exactly, the 14th of April, to be specific - for the needs of the SDA of Bosanski Samac, you brought in something from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never brought anything for the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you. I am thinking of the case when, together with Fuad Jasenica, you brought in weapons which were subsequently distributed in the TO building.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never brought in any weapons to Samac except my rifle, the one that I purchased outside Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I have the usher's assistance, please. Can they be marked for identification, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D9 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D9/2 ter ID and document D9/2 ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I do apologise. I was concerned that the document was being tendered into evidence and not merely marked for identification, but that's my mistake. I see that it is being marked for identification. I'm sorry for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salkic, would you please read the document out, slowly, from the beginning, please, the heading and everything else.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDA party, the Party of Democratic Action, the Municipal Board, Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Read it slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you'll read it out better than me, and I'll just say what the certificate is about. Read it instead of me. I don't see very well and I think you'll do a better job of it, and then I can say yes or no or to whatever you ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If the Court would allow me, I would like to read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall read it, then. The SDA, Party of Democratic Action, Municipal Board, Bosanski Samac, number -- blank. Date, the 14th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Have a look at the document in front of you, and you can say if what I'm reading out is what is written there. Tell me if I read something out wrongly. Bring my attention to that straight away, please: "Certificate for Jasenica, Fuad, son of Husein; and Salkic, Ibrahim, son of Meho, both from Bosanski Samac. This is to certify that the above named are authorised to communicate with relevant organs in the Republic of Croatia in the name of this board and for the purposes of acquiring or receipt of equipment against a receipt for the needs of the residents of Bosanski Samac. The above named are authorised to take over the agreed equipment." SDA, as a signature, the Municipal Board, and Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: Have I read this document out correctly?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one? No. This is the first time that I'm looking at it, the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I see. The first time. Thank you. Tell me, please: Do you know that Mr. Sulejman Tihic wrote a book called "Recollections" with respect to the events in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You don't know that he wrote a book like that?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You haven't read the book?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, Mr. Salkic, in that book Mr. Tihic explicitly says that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Counsel. I could be wrong, but it's my recollection when Mr. Sulejman Tihic was on the stand for examination-in-chief and wanted to introduce his so-called memories or memoirs, that there was an objection and he wasn't allowed to introduce them. As I say, I could be wrong, but I raise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You are right. Your Honour, but it wasn't me who objected.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No. It was the whole of the Defence team, from what I can recall. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: But despite that, there's also another matter that I think precludes the question. I can see where it was going, and was going to ask this man to comment on something that Sulejman Tihic wrote. And unless he's disgusted or has read the book or is aware and has aired his views, together with that of Mr. Tihic, you can't really expect him to answer anything about the book, given that the author is Mr. Tihic particularly, as he'll be here next. So on that basis also, I would object to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I just want to be clear in my mind: Is this the memoirs, or is this a book, different from the memoirs?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is the book named "Memoirs," by Sulejman Tihic, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: With due respect, Your Honours, I believe I'm entitled to ask the witness about the fact of his opinion about the certain fact which I am going to present to him or put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: He can say, "No, it's not true," and I will be more than happy to ask Sulejman Tihic about that, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is a book written by Mr. Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sulejman Tihic. That is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So how can he answer yes or no on the contents of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: He can say whether the facts which Mr. Sulejman Tihic is saying in his book are right or wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He doesn't know what research Mr. Tihic made.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He doesn't know what research Mr. Tihic made.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, but I'm going to read the facts about what Mr. Tihic was referring to, and he can say whether that is true or not, simple as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That can be done. There's no question that Mr. Zecevic can achieve his objective. But by putting it in the mouth of Mr. Tihic before he asks the question is what makes it objectionable. If Mr. Tihic says that the sun rises in the north and sets in the south, Mr. Zecevic can ask the witness if that's, in fact, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: According to the sun rising in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So he can put what Mr. Tihic -- what he may know or not know about what's in Mr. Tihic's book to the witness, but he mustn't put it on the basis of "This is what Tihic says. What do you say?" Because it's unfair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, instead of putting them as if they are facts --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- put the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Put the text or put the idea or put the fact or put the proposition to the witness, simple. And if that happens, then I've got no problem. And then --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a text before me. I can read it, and then the witness can give his opinion on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Not his opinion. He can only answer --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: His position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- whether he agrees or disagrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Whether it is right or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The SDA in Bosanski Samac received from Croatia, I think from Slavonski Brod, another shipment of weapons, quantity of weapons, about 50 automatic rifles, two mortars, several zoljas, hand-held rocket launchers and some ammunition. These weapons were brought by Fuad Jasenica and Ibrahim Salkic, and they obtained them on the basis of a receipt which I gave to them on behalf of the SDA. I did not believe that they would get the weapons, but they did bring them in. So I sent it to the TO staff, which was established two days before that. The bulk of the weapons were distributed immediately in the TO headquarters, mostly to Muslims and also a few weapons to Croats." If I understood you correctly, Mr. Salkic, what is written in this book is not correct. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is quite certain. It is not correct. That is his -- he wrote that, and I am telling you the truth. I never saw this receipt or certificate, ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am asking you about the facts set out here.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps those weapons were brought in, but I was not present nor did I have anything to do with it. But I can't say that it didn't actually take place. What I'm saying is that I did not take part in it. I received no certificate or receipt. I did not bring in any weapons, nor do I know whether any weapons were in fact brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, Mr. Salkic: You said that you were arrested on the 18th of April; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that you were then put into the TO building on the 19th of April, which is to say, the following day?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you were incarcerated there until the 26th of April, when you were transferred to Brcko; is that right? I didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in those seven days that you spent in the Territorial Defence building, with you were the Bicic brothers, Dragan Lukac, Izet Izetbegovic, and several other people; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were taken a few times to have lunch at the Utva factory, right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Breakfast or lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: A meal?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, twice, in the morning and in the afternoon. So there were not three meals, there were two, and we went for the first two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You testified here that on one occasion when you were in Utva, you saw Milan Simic; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the transcript dated November 1st, you said, on page 3288, lines 17 through 19, that you had the feeling that he was embarrassed because all of you were people that he knew well. Is that the way you put it?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You meant you and the Bicic brothers; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all of those who were present, because he knew quite a few of the people there. Samac is a small town.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Salkic, did you make any comments with regard to this with the other people who were standing in the line with you?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you couldn't really talk very much, so I doubt that there were many comments there. You'd just eat what there was, keep your head down, and then back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: However, they could certainly have seen him, too, if you managed to see him?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the first moment, when a few of us walked in, the first ones, the gentleman was standing there. Since I worked in that company for a few years, I know that very well. If necessary, I'm going to describe that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No. There is no need for that. I'm just asking whether others could see him as well.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them, yes, some who…

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were in Brcko from the 27th of April until the 1st of May; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, something around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You also testified that in Brcko you were detained in two rooms?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: With you in the same room were the Bicic brothers, who were also detained, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can remember the people who were with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, tell us, then.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Dragan Lukac, Mersad Gibic, Dragan Delic, then a little guy called Legija. There were about 30 of us, 35 at the maximum. I can't remember at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said on November 1st, page 3300, line 19, that you saw Simic in Brcko as he was standing in the vicinity of the building where you were detained; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the same transcript, a page later, line 8, you said that whenever you would see someone, it would give rise to your hopes that you would go home; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the same page, Mr. Salkic, line 25, you stated that what you saw was very brief, only a few minutes, or rather, a minute and a half and two?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that then they left?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You saw Milan Simic, you said, together with Topcagic and Djuheric?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djuheric, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you share that with someone in your room?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All of you who were detained in that room?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that room and in the room next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Next to it?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, everyone. Everybody was looking forward to good news that we were going home, because Brcko was already a free town, free, and then your hopes go high. You hope that you'll be released.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you sure that the others saw him too?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot assert anything on behalf of anyone else, but the five or six of us or whatever who were at the windows could see this quite clearly. Some could not get up due to the injuries that they had, and they could not see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Tell me, in your statement of the 7th and 9th of November in 1995 that you gave to the OTP, you did not mention that you saw Milan Simic in Utva and in Brcko; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I thought that that was unimportant, that what was important was only what would come in the following description. However, in the additional explanation, I realised that that had to be mentioned too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'll get to that too. You are aware of the fact that Milan Simic voluntarily surrendered to the Tribunal in February 1998; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You gave your statement to the investigators of the OTP immediately after this event, that is to say, on the 10th of March, 1998; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [In English] If the Court pleases, I can mark this for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a statement of this same witness given to the OTP back in 1998 on the 10th of March, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 1998, yes. We can have it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D10/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We have the English translation as well, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have. It's on the ELMO, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The English translation will be D10/2 ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salkic, take a look. Is this your statement?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but I can see straight away that there is a mistake, because I and Mr. Simic never worked together.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to put a question to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Salkic, this is your statement, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You gave this statement voluntarily of your own free will, without any coercion involved; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to turn to page 3 of the statement, that is, the next page.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only there is one thing that I just cannot understand. I just have to ask you about this. Just as I thought that this is a mistake, then this is also a mistake too. What does "Rdovno" mean, R-d-o-v-n-o? What does that mean, Bosnia and Serbia and Croatia? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It must be a typo.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then, there was another mistake, too, concerning Simic. What can I say?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Witness, the Prosecution is following. If there are any problems, the Prosecution will deal with that. Now, for the time being, counsel is simply cross-examining. So you simply do as he says. You turn to the page, to the paragraph, and he'll be asking you questions. So you simply answer the questions as he asks them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind as to look at the next page and to read these two sentences out, the ones that are highlighted in the second paragraph, please. The second paragraph, page number 3. See, it's on the bottom of the page, page number 3. Would you please be so kind as to read that.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I also saw Milan Simic on one occasion in Brcko. He came together with Simo Zaric but was waiting outside while Zaric was questioning us."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, Mr. Salkic, that is your statement, that is what you stated then, if you'll remember?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then you asserted that he came with Mr. Zaric, and you did not mention Fadil Topcagic and Djuheric; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When my -- what should I call him? Rather, the Prosecutor, when he asked me to describe this event in greater detail, then I did so, and then I remembered that several people were present there, and that is what I told the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me something else: You said then that Mr. Simic was waiting for Zaric, and in your statement -- or rather, while you were testifying last Thursday, you said that it was only between a minute and a half and two; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, please allow me to speak a bit. I cannot just say "correct" or "incorrect." I have to explain this sentence, if you'll allow me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Of course I'll allow you to do that, but just please answer my question. Of course I'm going to allow you to explain.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Mr. Simic with Zaric, but Zaric walked into the building and the three gentlemen remained outside. And they were there very briefly, as I said, and they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's not what it says in that statement dated February 1998 -- March 1998, rather.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not explained in detail like now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since this is one of the stipulations we made with the Prosecution, you know that Mr. Simic was appointed only on the 30th of May, 1992 to be head of the Executive Council. Don't you know that?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that. I learned about that only later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, Mr. Salkic: You are the best friend of Muhamed and Hasan Bicic; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are my best friends, and I'm probably their best friend too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You came to their pizzeria; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's where you saw Milan Simic from time to time; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the transcript dated the 31st of October, page 3189, line 15 and further on, you said: "From time to time we would meet at the cafe, here and there. It could be said that we were on good terms. Because Samac is a small town, everybody knew everybody. It's not a big city. We socialised, and sometimes when I would need something, he would do me a favour."

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is that what you stated, exactly?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Further on, on page 3190, line 19, you said -- in response to a question related to the relationship between Hasan and Muhamed Bicic and Milan Simic, you answered the following to the Prosecutor: "Yes. They would often meet at the pizzeria that the Bicics had. They met and talked. Actually, I think that they were on much better terms with him than me." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You never worked together with Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. That's some kind of a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were not a close, intimate friend of his?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how people see this, but whenever we would see each other, we would say hello to each other, chat a bit, have a drink. So I don't know to what extent you think that this should be. I mean, for me that was enough. This was friends.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please pause between putting the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Remember to pause. I know you get --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You get taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I have to repeat the question. I'm sorry, Mr. Salkic. When I say "close, intimate friends," I mean did you confide in each other, did you go to see him at home?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, may I please have the statement again, the previous one of March 10, 1998, the second page, and put the English on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Salkic: Over there on page 1, could you please read this.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Milan Simic and I before the war were close friends. We worked together ..." This is a mistake. We did not work together. We socialised, "... for periods and met on a regular basis." That's okay. Why don't you go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In that statement, it says that you were intimate friends and that you worked together.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That we worked together, no. That's some kind of a mistake, just like over here, see. But we did not work together, not ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So that's not what you said to the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a mistake, maybe a typographical error or whatever, like over here, see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was this statement read out to you?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I didn't really pay attention to every little word, on what terms I was with Milan, you know. For me, this was a good relationship, that we would meet, say hello to each other, chat, have a drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now let us deal with what happened at the primary school. Mr. Salkic, in the transcript dated the 2nd of November, page 48, line 12 of the unofficial transcript - because we still haven't got the official transcript - you said that this event took place in mid-June, sometime around 10.00 in the evening, that it was dark but there was moonlight, so you could discern things; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's what you said?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Salkic: At that time in Samac there wasn't any electricity; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Not at all?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't have any over there. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on in the transcript, on the same day, on page 33, line 1 and further on, you said -- in response to the Prosecutor's question whether anybody could go into the gym at any time, you answered the following: "Anyone. Serbs, civilians came, even some women came to beat us, soldiers, policemen. Whenever anyone wanted to come in, the door would simply open and they would walk in and beat us." Is that what you stated?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, Mr. Salkic: These people who walked in like that to beat you, they didn't have uniforms or did they come on some kind of official business; they simply felt like beating someone and they would walk in?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely, just the way you put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I assume that it is your assumption that the guards allowed that; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: While giving your -- while testifying, in response to the Prosecutor's questions related to one of the photographs -- [In English] F59, please, the photograph by the Prosecutor. I don't know which is the evidence number, but it's P -- F --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: P14A.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: F59 I believe it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: P14A.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: P14A. I'm sorry. Thank you. [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. Salkic. [In English] If you can put it on the ELMO. That's the one, yes. Show it to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember this photograph?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Salkic: When the Prosecutor showed you this photograph, you said that you were sitting in the right-hand corner, viewed from the entrance into the gym itself. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can show this to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's here. It's this small part that's missing. If we were to extend it a bit on this side, it would be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is the right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you enter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you enter the gym. The gym did not look this way then; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. There were parts of that Swedish ladder over there, and there were some -- there are some things there now than what is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, it was in better condition than this dilapidated room that you can see now?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. The difference is not considerable. It's only the Swedish ladder that's missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the usher to show to the witness P30/1 ter. [Interpretation] I'm going to show you another diagram that the Prosecutor showed you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You can put it on the ELMO, please, the one which the witness did draw something on. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the drawing that the Prosecutor showed you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you -- would you show me in this drawing in which part of the gym you were sitting, if that's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a magic marker --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can we do this on this copy, or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've got no objection, as long as it's clearly delineated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. If we can use a different colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Different colour and a different -- and perhaps lettering or something like that instead of numbering, something to make it distinct and clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Distinct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Numbers, okay. Or would you agree that we put the letters?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Anything, as long as it's distinct and clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe you can put the witness' initials there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sure. I've got no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be so kind as to put your initials at the place where, in your opinion, you were, roughly.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Salkic. Tell me, please, if you remember: Who was sitting next to you, on one side and on the other side?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were the two Bicic brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just tell me who was sitting next to you, right next to you.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two Bicic brothers were by me. I think that on one side was Muhamed and on the other side -- well, I don't know whether he was here or there now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm just asking you if you remember.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at any rate, the Bicics were right there by me, and also there was Srna. I think his first name was Safet. He was there by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember Silvestar Antunovic?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Silvestar was a bit further away, and he lay there immobile, and now -- while he was there, but now whether he was there on that particular moment, I can't confirm that. He was taken to Belgrade. I don't know exactly which date.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you about the position.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, you know, can you give us a better explanation? If Muhamed and Hasan are on your left and right, where was Silvestar Antunovic in relation to Muhamed?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Silvestar was on our right-hand side as we were standing or lying there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The first one next to Muhamed?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I can't remember that exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, if you remember: Who was sitting next to the door or right behind the door?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first it was Omer Nalic right by the door, on the Swedish block, and then he left, and then there was Dragan Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to bother you any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Salkic: In the transcript dated the 2nd of November, page 49, line 23 and 24, you said: "Many of us recognised his voice," and you were referring to Milan Simic; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you did not clearly see him and recognise him. It was the voice.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was at the entrance into the gym. He shouted that we should get up because a Serb minister was coming in, and then what followed, as I have described it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that's when you recognised him by his voice; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By then, I already saw him as he walked in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You say that he introduced himself as a Serb minister; right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A minister in the government, the Serb government.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I imagine that he was speaking loudly as he walked in?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So that other detainees could also hear him?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, when people could really focus, because everybody was so afraid, and if they could really hear things.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you very kindly to answer my questions, if that's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but, you know, I can't explain things to you if I do not answer with additional matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I asked you whether others --

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could hear, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then five of you were called out; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You, the Bicic brothers, Perica Misic, and Mersad Gibic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you went out into the corridor, there was a candle burning and they had flashlights; is that right? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember who was holding the flashlight?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [In English] If I could have the assistance of the usher again, I'm sorry, about this. It's the same P30/1 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, if you happen to remember, Mr. Salkic, where the candle was.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The candle was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the ELMO, please, Mr. Salkic.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were big windows here, and they were raised about 1 metre 30, 40 above ground, and they were standing on the window ledge there. And there was another one here on the table where the guards were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On this document, you marked the place where you were standing and the order in which you were lined up along the wall, the crosses on the right; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've said that. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So that is between the guard bench and the corner of that room?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Salkic, the guards who were on duty in the corridor, did they sit at that table?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention to them. I didn't really notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But usually? Would you say they usually sat there?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, the wall you were lined up against, facing the boiler room, it was half brick and half glass; is that right? There was a glass partition above the bricks?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's return to the events now and focus on them. You testified that Simic said some nonsensical things and started from Perica Misic and ordered you to spread your legs, and he then kicked you with his knee in the groin, in the genitals; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: His escorts would then continue to beat you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly to say that he kicked each of you four in the genitals with his knee?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he kicked me once. As far as I was able to notice, he didn't do this to the rest, but he repeated it several times to the people standing behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And he then slapped you?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It wasn't anything that terrible compared to the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said "mildly." It wasn't interpreted. Did you say "mildly"?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It wasn't a strong slap. It was a slap, but he didn't actually beat me very hard. I don't -- there might be a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, no misunderstanding. I was thinking of the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it wasn't a strong blow. It was a mild, light slap.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether he slapped each of you? If you remember, Mr. Salkic. Only if you remember.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't tell you now. I really couldn't say at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did he seem to you to be under the effects of alcohol, Mr. Simic? Was he drunk?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I still have that dilemma today. I'm still troubled by that dilemma.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. May I be allowed to comment? May I be allowed to comment? I'm not going to say anything terrible. Had he been drunk, I would have found it easier at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is that the dilemma that you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, on the transcript of the 2nd of November, page 53, line 1 goes on to say -- you said that you, and I mean all of you, that his escorts proceeded to beat all of you with metal bars on your chest, and Muhamed received three or four blows because he tried to dodge. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's what you said?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On that same page of the transcript, you said, "Simic stood over there, and behind him was a man with a weapon of some kind. They shot above Perica's and Hasan's head." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, if I remember correctly, Hasan was closest to the entrance. Would you take a look at the floor plan? He was closest to the entrance where it says "F57." Is that the cross denoting Perica Misic?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because Gibic had gone inside. There was Perica, Hasan, Muhamed, and then me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, did you see who did the shooting, who fired?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm in a dilemma now. Those are the kinds of things that one has a dilemma over. Now, can I just say I'm not thinking of anything bad? I don't wish to confirm something at any point which is not true, not correct, and I hope you'll understand me, the Defence counsel and the Prosecution and the Trial Chamber, when I say this, that I am faced with a dilemma. So I'm not going to say something I'm not absolutely certain of. So once again, I can say that I'm not certain of who fired, although others said who it was, but I didn't actually see it taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you allow for the possibility that somebody else standing behind Milan Simic might have done the firing?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, I didn't see it actually happen, so I don't want to confirm or claim something that I didn't actually see. I was a participant. I could join those who thought that way and said that, but I didn't see it, and even if I think that I might -- that it might have happened that way, I don't want to say that I actually saw it, because I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, please, a moment ago, you said that Perica and Hasan were closer to the corner. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The bullet that was fired ended up in the ceiling, the wall, somewhere above their heads; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You then saw Simic going out with his escorts; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So that means you were still lined up in the hallway of the school when he came out?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He went out, and some of them went out, but not everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about him.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Simic went out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In that same transcript dated the 2nd of November, page 54 of the unofficial transcript, line 22 and 23, you stated the following: "I -- we thought they were finished, and then Muhamed asked whether anybody had been wounded." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Then you were sent back into the gym; is that right? And you said that you were standing the whole night, singing, following orders from the guards?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who stayed on with Mr. Simic who were last, who went out last with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But what I'm saying is that somebody ordered you to do that and you had to stand all night and sing; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Nobody offered you any assistance, any compresses of any kind?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only what we had amongst ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm saying did you help each other?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we wouldn't be here now if we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I mean on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then you said, "Five to seven days later, Milan returned, brought out Hasan and Perica, Perica Misic, and they returned somewhere at dawn." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On that same transcript dated the 2nd of November, page 58, line 20 onwards, you said that they told you they had changed clothes, that they talked to Milan, and you said, "I think that he sent us two cartons of cigarettes."

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that "He told them to apologise to me, Muhamed and Mersad Gibic." That's what you said here; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, why apologies to Mersad Gibic when he was sent back to the gym and not beaten?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was beaten. He got his share, inside when he was taken out, but not by Mr. Milan Simic over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, Mr. Milan Simic did not beat him. He wasn't beaten by Mr. Milan Simic in the gym?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I have to comment. Make I make my comment? Can I comment now? He was beaten in the hallway or corridor in between. There is a middle corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But a moment ago you said that he wasn't beaten by Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't when we were brought out here, when we were taken out here, and that's why I crossed him out there. But he probably thought that it was his turn to apologise, which was nice of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just let's clear up one point, please. Mersad Gibic, was he beaten by Milan Simic or not; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You mean by Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But let me explain. Let me explain where.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please, go ahead and explain.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see this passageway here, from the entrance moving this way? He was brought here, and then he was returned inside, straight away. Somebody kicked him with his leg and said, "Go inside," told him to go inside. That means that only the four of us remained standing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [In English] Could I just have a minute, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Sorry, could I just seek a clarification? You were asked, "Was he beaten by Milan Simic; yes or no?" And you said yes. "You mean by Milan Simic?" You say yes again. Is that your answer, that he was beaten by Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mersad Gibic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mersad Gibic. He beat Mersad Gibic, who was returned, sent back to the gym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: It's just that earlier at 1813, I think you said that, "No, he was not beaten by him."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He did not beat him at this place here, in this position, this spot, that I indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just to complete the clarification, where, in which area, did he beat him, did Mr. Milan Simic beat him? If you can point out with your pointer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That was here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Indicating the entrance hall - thank you - to the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you put a mark at the spot where this happened, a circle with a cross inside, please, if you can remember where this happened.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean where Mr. Milan took -- beat Gibic? It was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did he beat anybody else there?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in passing, because Gibic came out first. That's why he stood there in the hallway first.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Salkic, in 1995, or more exactly on the 7th and the 9th of February, you gave a statement to the investigators. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There were three investigators, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You don't remember?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know there were three. Now, whether one of them was an interpreter or not, I don't know. But there were three people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right, three people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Put it on the ELMO, please, the first page. The cover page, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, please, Mr. Salkic: Have a look at the statement. It's your own statement.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And take a look at the screen, and you'll see signatures. Is that your signature among them?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On each of the pages you placed your initials. You initialed each page; is that right? Take a look at the English version, please. Turn the page and have a look at the pages, each of them. It's a bad copy?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Can you help me out here? I don't know what you're asking me about. I see my initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I just want you to confirm whether that is your statement and your signature.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The statement is 13 pages long; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, have a look at the Serbian text.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please: At that time, your memory was much fresher, in view of the fact that you were exchanged a year and a half before you gave this statement; is that right? Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you can't say that. I can say whether I felt okay or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you whether you felt all right or not; I asked you whether your memory, your recollections were clearer then than they are now. You said then rather than now.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all right. Continue with your questioning. I don't -- I see that my opinions aren't important.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you: Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My memories are always very clear in my mind when I think back to those events, the events that took place and the things that I experienced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Witness. Please remember to pause, and please don't be rude to counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to turn to page 8 of your statement and take a look at the last paragraph on page 8. And it has been marked in yellow. The passage has been marked in yellow. Have you found it, Mr. Salkic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's the number 8 in English version as well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you read that whole paragraph out, please.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will do that and I will listen carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Then please give me the statement back.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was shorter, I would be happy to read it out, but like this --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's fine. Just leave it with the witness so he can check it out whether it's right or not. Just bear with me, Your Honours. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You check to see if I'm reading out correctly: "Stevo Todorovic would enter the gym and we would have to sing Serbian songs. As he was the police chief, Stevo, with his bodyguards, sometimes four or five, including Goran Hasic, Goran Ristic, and Slobo Vakic, would start by -- would start from Omer Nalic and then move on to the others, to the rest of us. He would ask whether we had any children and said that we would no longer have them any more, and things like that. We were made to stand with our legs spread and he would kick us in the balls. When you fell down, the others would beat you and he would move. Kissing his boot was another demand, as a 'Serbian boot walking Serbian land.' He would kick kneeling prisoners, and then we had to thank him for teaching us how to respect the Serbian chief and Serbian people. Todorovic would then make a second round of the gym and would always choose specific prisoners. As far as I recall, besides myself, the victims were Behrem Masic, the brothers," whose name has been deleted, "the Bicic brothers, [redacted] and Omer Nalic. The others who were with Stevo would carry on with the beatings until the victims fell unconscious." Have I read that out correctly, your statement?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely as it happened, just the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you explained to us here the way in which Stevan Todorovic and his entourage beat you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: He beat all of you like that, including Muhamed Bicic?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he would rarely miss him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Rarely miss him?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think he was always beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Salkic: You make no mention of Milan Simic in that statement anywhere, not a single word.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said last time --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, if Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't object to the question if Mr. Zecevic is asking whether there's any mention of Milan Simic in that paragraph, nor do I object if he's --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Not the paragraph; the whole statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The whole statement. That's right. Now, as long as that's specified and made clear to the witness, because I wasn't clear, and I think that's important that that be clarified. Otherwise, I have no objection, just subject to that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot follow the translation, but I did ask: Have you had -- mentioned Milan Simic in this statement? That is exactly what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I said: in the statement.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in that statement, but in the other statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "the other statement," do you mean the March 1998 statement?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Salkic: In this 1995 statement that you have in front of you, you make no mention, as you have said, of the Utva and Brcko sites, nor do you mention the beating of the four of you.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You mean you don't mention them?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this one. Probably not. I don't know. I would have to read through it, but I don't think so, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You don't mention the shooting and firing that you took -- that you mentioned above the head of your own brother when you thought at one moment that he might be killed. You don't make any mention of that either.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So all these events appear in the statement of the 10th of March, 1998?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when that second statement was, what the date was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you like to take a look at it?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There's no need. I said what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm asking you now: The events that I enumerated a moment ago appear the first time in the 1998 statement?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's when the investigators came. I saw fit to tell them then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What made you think that this was a fit occasion to tell them then?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just so that that was -- that became common knowledge, that this truth should out [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it has nothing to do with Milan Simic's surrender in 1998, did it?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's how I got the idea to state what I had seen. It brought it to mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I have just one more question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Salkic: Before this Trial Chamber, you said a moment ago that your memory is equally fresh at all times; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 10 of the transcript dated the 2nd of November, having described this event in the primary school in its entirety and Mr. Simic's departure, asked by the Prosecutor whether anybody used a weapon or instrument of any kind, your answer was: "Yes. As I have already said, when they prepared to leave, they were at the entrance or exit. I forgot to say that." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who do you mean was at the exit? Are you reading that or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm reading from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that case I meant Todorovic, Simic, and the escorts, because he said they were his escorts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I completely agree, but I'm just asking you: You said, "I forgot that." Were those your words? Did you say you had forgotten it, and the Prosecutor reminded you of it?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I forgot to say that. I forgot to say what took place as they were going out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Salkic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'd like to know whether the other counsel would like to cross-examine. I can see Mr. Lukic shaking his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on behalf of my colleague Mr. Pisarevic, I can say that both of us will be examining the witness. It will take about half an hour. Maybe my colleagues will take a little longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We shall adjourn now, and we shall resume tomorrow morning at 0930 hours, hopefully, if we have all the services that are required for these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I wonder, if Your Honours please, if Mr. Pisarevic could give us a brief indication. It's just for purposes of getting Mr. Tihic here. We don't want him sitting around for too long. If we start at 9.30 and we know that Mr. Lukic is going to be about half an hour, if Mr. Pisarevic could indicate about how long he will be, that would enable us to get Mr. Tihic here at a more reasonable hour. He's been driving a long time, I think, and it would be ideal to ensure that he's not here at -- that he's here at a more appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I intend to cross-examine Mr. Salkic for at least one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So Mr. Tihic can be brought after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Court will rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 6th day of November, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.35 p.m.,
